candidate: checkpoint plus requirement accounting and enabled regression
expected: The inner call is guarded by First. Its InnerOnly alternative must not widen the wrapper's First | Second domain or produce an incompatible-argument error for this valid call.

`FUNCTION inner` argument `which` has an incompatible type
expected: First | InnerOnly

source_attribution: DirectSummaryCompiler::push_formal_projection only qualifies descendant Field steps; project_value and project_interned_formal_value return unchanged whole-value inputs for empty paths.

legacy_oracle.entrypoint: boon_typecheck::check_program after boon_parser::parse_source; test-only legacy-owner-oracle dependency
legacy_oracle.verification: The enabled regression asserts both empty legacy diagnostics and the exact First | Second wrapper domain before running the candidate. Fresh execution passes those assertions and fails the candidate no-errors assertion. Acceptance alone is not used as proof of narrowing.

control.source_change: Replace inner(which: which) with inner(which: First), leaving the rest of the source unchanged.
control.purpose: Diagnostic isolation only; not a production workaround or performance observation.

negative_control.status: enabled failing regression; current candidate loses an error retained by both older checks
negative_control.discarded_control: An inner function matching only InnerOnly was not a valid legacy-negative oracle: the legacy checker widened its inferred formal to First | InnerOnly while narrowing the guarded actual to First. The numeric requirement provides the independent negative control instead.

limitations: K0 CLI reports diagnostic count, not diagnostic bytes, and runs client role while the integration regressions use server role. Exact cross-version diagnostic parity is not established here. Principal FormalRead and expression_requirement_variable also lack arm guards; a summary-only change is not a complete fix. The numeric false-negative has not yet been bisected to a specific K1 commit.
